# PR-head review threads for acme/widget#82 (N=1) ## Setup and query owner **Aliases:** - `ROOT=/work/widget` - `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` - `H=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`, the pre-rework head - `B=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, origin/main Provisioning and the base merge are already done; this covers only the thread fetch. **Query owner:** both queries come from `reference/pr-head.md` § "Fetch unresolved review threads". They are cited here, not copied. - **Q1** is the paginated `reviewThreads` query, with its own `endCursor`. - **Q2** is the per-thread `node(id:)` comments query, with a separate comment cursor. The process cwd stays at the primary checkout throughout. Nothing runs `cd`. | # | Command (cwd = ROOT, no `cd`) | Purpose | |---|---|---| | C1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fetch all reviewThreads pages | | C2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='' -F id=` | Fetch T1's comments, starting at its first comment page | This runs per admitted PR. N=1 is included, so only #82 is queried. ## Successful fetch **C1 result.** - C1 returned three pages, which were merged into T1, T2, TX and T3. - I then filtered to `isResolved == false`. TX (`src/gone.ts:2`) is resolved, so it is dropped. - T1's comments report `hasNextPage: true` with `totalCount=102`, which exceeds the 100-comment first page. That triggers C2. **C2 result.** - C2 runs on T1's own comment cursor, separate from the reviewThreads cursor. It continues until `hasNextPage` is false. - Page 1 returns comment 1 (the first request) plus replies 1–99. - Page 2 returns replies 100–101. - T1's initial 100 comments are replaced by this complete 102-comment connection, so nothing is duplicated. - T2 and T3 have no further comment pages, so no follow-up query is needed for them. **Location rule:** - Use `:` when `line` is set. - Otherwise use `: (outdated)`. - Otherwise use the bare ``. All comments carry the same supplied metadata: - url: `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1` - author: `reviewer` - createdAt: `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` Every comment below is listed in its original order. | Thread | Location | Comments in order | Effective request | |---|---|---|---| | T1 | `src/retry.ts:12` | 1. "Rewrite the retry engine"
2–101. replies 1–100: "Rewrite still requested"
102. reply 101: "Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines." | Changed by the final reply: **keep the engine and cap retries in two lines.** The rewrite is withdrawn. | | T2 | `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)` (`line=null`, `originalLine=7`) | 1. "Keep this guard"
2. "Yes, retain it" | Keep the guard. The reply confirms it. | | T3 | `README.md` (`line=null`, `originalLine=null`) | 1. "Document the cap" | Document the retry cap. | **Record carried to gather (#82):** ```text Threads (3 unresolved): - T1 src/retry.ts:12 — keep engine; cap retries in two lines (reply 101 corrects the original "Rewrite the retry engine") - T2 src/old.ts:7 (outdated) — keep this guard (confirmed) - T3 README.md — document the cap ``` I read every reply, not just the first request. That is why T1's actionable request is the two-line cap rather than the rewrite. ## Failed fetch (independent case) C1, or C2 for any thread, returns `API unavailable`. I stop before gather and before the spec. No draft is written, no record is made, and nothing continues past this point. This applies even though this is an N=1 run. ```text threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable) ``` The worktree `W` is left as provisioned, on `fix/retry` at the merged head. Nothing is pushed. Finish has its own separate rule for reporting fetch failures after verification; that rule does not apply here. ## Empty set (independent case) C1 succeeds, and after merging pages and filtering there are zero unresolved threads. No C2 is needed. ```text Threads: none ``` Flow then continues to gather with: - `PR: acme/widget#82` - `Pre-rework head: H` - `Base SHA: bbbbbbb`

I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill’s PR-head review-thread procedure. Provisioning and base-merge narration are omitted as requested. ### Command and metadata legends - `ROOT=/work/widget`; `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`. - PR values: owner `acme`, repository `widget`, number `82`. - Query/pagination owner: **`using-git-worktrees/reference/pr-head.md`, “Fetch unresolved review threads.”** - `QT` means that owner’s exact reviewThreads query; `QC` means its exact thread-comments query. These are command-argument aliases, not replacement queries. - Every command below runs with **cwd `$W`**. No real commands are executed here. - Every rendered comment carries metadata **M**: `url=https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`, `author=reviewer`, `createdAt=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. - `C(text)` denotes one comment with that exact body and all metadata M. A numbered range denotes each individual comment, in order—not a summary replacing comments. ### Successful fetch: commands in order | Order | Exact command arguments | Result / resolved values | |---|---|---| | 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fetch and merge all **three reviewThreads pages**, using that connection’s `endCursor`. Page 1: unresolved `T1`; page 2: unresolved `T2`, resolved `TX`; page 3: unresolved `T3`. Filter out `TX`. | | 2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QC" -F id=T1` | `T1` has `totalCount=102` and initial `hasNextPage=true`. Start its follow-up query at the **first comment page**, paginate with its own separate `endCursor`, and replace—not append to—the initial comments connection with all 102 comments. | The initial T1 comment page holds the opening comment and replies 1–99. Its later comment page holds replies 100–101, including the correction. Review-thread and comment cursors remain separate. T2 and T3 need no comment follow-up. ### Successful rendering | Thread / location | Complete ordered comments | |---|---| | **T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`** | Comment 1: `C(Rewrite the retry engine)`.
Comments 2–101, respectively replies 1–100: each is `C(Rewrite still requested)`.
Comment 102, reply 101: `C(Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.)` | | **T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`** | Comment 1: `C(Keep this guard)`.
Comment 2: `C(Yes, retain it)` | | **T3 — `README.md`** | Comment 1: `C(Document the cap)` | Each expanded comment retains M individually, including all 100 identical T1 replies. Resolved `TX` at `src/gone.ts:2` is excluded. **Current repair requests, after reading every reply:** retain the retry engine and cap retries in two lines; retain the outdated-location guard; document the cap. The late T1 correction supersedes the earlier rewrite request. Fetching is complete; gather may proceed. ### Independent failed fetch Starting independently from the provisioned singleton, run, at cwd `$W`: ```sh gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82 ``` Result: `API unavailable`. **Stop:** `threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)` This N=1 run stops **before gather and spec**. No draft, continuation record, or comment follow-up is produced. ### Independent successful empty fetch Starting independently, run the same command at cwd `$W`: ```sh gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82 ``` After successful pagination and unresolved filtering, render: ```text Threads: none ``` No comment follow-up is needed; gather may proceed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither fact moved. Both outputs cite reference/pr-head.md as the query owner, merge all three reviewThreads pages, drop resolved TX, keep T1/T2/T3 comments in order with the supplied url/author/createdAt, re-fetch T1's 102 comments by thread id on a separate comment cursor until the last page and replace rather than append (no duplicates), and read reply 101 as the correction to a two-line retry cap. After actually improves on Before by naming node(id:) explicitly for Q2, which Before only implied via '-F id=<T1 id>'; keep that. After's only soft spot on the threads fact is that it drops Before's explicit sentence that the correction lives only on a later comment page so reviewThreads pagination alone would miss it—retain a line like 'reply 101 is only reachable through C2; the reviewThreads pages alone would show T1 as a rewrite request' to make the insufficiency claim textual rather than inferred. On locations-failure both render src/retry.ts:12, src/old.ts:7 (outdated), README.md, both emit the exact 'threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)' stop with no draft/record continuation and the N=1 caveat, and both render 'Threads: none' for the empty case. Two minor After wording cautions unrelated to the facts: the failed-fetch note says W is 'at the merged head' while setup says H is the pre-rework head—prefer 'at H with B already an ancestor' as Before did—and the empty-case 'Base SHA: bbbbbbb' abbreviates a SHA the brief asked to alias as B; use the alias.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved: both outputs name the pr-head.md query/pagination owner, paginate all three reviewThreads pages, drop resolved TX, render every T1/T2/T3 comment in order with the shared metadata M, fetch T1's comments by thread id with a separate comment cursor through the last page using replace-not-append, read reply 101 after replies 1-100 and carry the correction as a two-line cap rather than a rewrite, and both render src/retry.ts:12, src/old.ts:7 (outdated), README.md, the failed-fetch stop 'threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)' before gather and spec with no draft/record continuation, and 'Threads: none' for the empty fetch. The only wording risk in After is the added sentence asserting the first T1 comment page holds replies 1-99 and the later page holds 100-101: the input only says the correction (reply 101) is on a later page, so this invents a page boundary not in the supplied data. To keep the Change (routing via pr-head.md, explicit cwd=$W targeting) without that exposure, state only what the input gives—'the initial page is truncated (hasNextPage=true); reply 101's correction is on a later comment page'—and otherwise keep After's structure as is.
